notes: Default constructor: zeroes the vector words (+0x04..+0x0c) and constructs the mutex (+0x10), as the asm does. Does not write the bank count at +0 (asm checked), so bank_count_ has no initializer. Keeps the original's temporary one-bank manager built and destroyed. No callers in vox code.
C2 of the default constructor; same body and same unwritten bank count word as C1 (0x869858).

Sets the flag byte at +0x144 to 1 and copies the state name into the +0x146 buffer (strcpy, asm checked). No lock, as in the original. The buffer is unbounded and no vox-audio code reads it back, so a std::string keeps the same content. Deviation: a null name crashes the original in strcpy; the port stores an empty string.

Constructor: fades, the four id counters at 1, priority bank (8), default 3D parameters. The intrusive list sentinel at +0x43c/+0x440 starts empty (list_head_ and list_tail_ are null for the original's self-pointing sentinel). The word at +0x598 (side_buffer_) and +0x59c (side_word_) are zeroed. Only this constructor and the destructor touch those words in the binary (scan of all Hex-Rays bodies).
C2 constructor: same body as C1 (0x869a94), including the list sentinel and the +0x598/+0x59c words.

Destructor in the original order: data release, sub-decoder Clean, priority bank and driver destruction, FileSystemInterface::DestroyInstance, free of the +0x598 buffer when non-null, static instance cleared, then the nodes of the +0x43c list freed (each next word read before its node is freed). The list is never filled in the binary, so the loop is empty in practice.
Compiler-generated deleting destructor around D1 (0x86be68), which is now reconstructed; delete provides the variant.
Complete-object destructor, same body as D1 (0x86be68).

Constructor: base constructor, vtable, sentinel, window and raw value, total weight 0, reinsert flag 0 (asm checked). The asm never writes +0x38, +0x44, +0x50 or +0x54, and the port's header now has no initializer for them, so they keep whatever the caller's storage held (NativePlaylist::AddGroup gets the 0x5c bytes from VoxAlloc without zeroing). The default constructor (port only) sets them explicitly.

Saved values restored, window reinsert path, unlink and free as in the listing. Missing item: the reinsert path with an empty removed list and a positive exclusion window. The original then takes the sentinel's element-count word (+0x38) as the element pointer and reads through it (asm: the unlink dereferences the count); the port reads the sentinel's null element slot. The binary defines no value for that path.
Deletes the singleton through its virtual destructor and VoxFree, then clears s_voxEngine (as the listing does). Its destructor (0x862990) is reconstructed now.
D1: Shutdown, then the VoxEngineInternal object destroyed and freed (its destructor 0x86be68 is reconstructed now), then the mutex destroyed and freed. Order matches the listing.
